summary: Isle au Haut Light on Robinson Point, Maine: a fourth-order light lit 30 December 1907, automated in 1933-34, tower owned by the town, keeper's house now private.

lens.status: original optic; a fifth-order lens followed after automation (LighthouseFriends)

structures.type: conical granite base with cylindrical brick shaft

access.note: Tower owned by the Town of Isle au Haut; grounds open; dwelling and tower closed. Reached by ferry from Stonington and a walk. The keeper's house is a private residence.

facts.agency: Town of Isle au Haut (tower); keeper's house privately owned

events.note: Congress appropriated $14,000 on 23 June 1906 (NRHP); the Friends give $14,400. Two-acre site bought from Charles Robinson the same year.
Fourth-order light established 30 December 1907 (the notice; NRHP 'activated').
Granite-based brick tower, keeper's house, oil house, boathouse and fuel house.
Fourth-order Fresnel lens (USLHS: original optic).
Bell struck by machinery established (LighthouseFriends).
Harry Smith succeeded Elmer F. Holbrook.
LighthouseFriends dates automation to 29 June 1933; the nomination and the Society give 1934 (see notes).
Automated; buildings except the tower sold (NRHP; USLHS 'Year Automated: 1934').
Characteristic changed from fixed white and fixed red to flashing red at automation (LighthouseFriends).
Keeper's house bought back by Charles Robinson with Senator Margaret Chase Smith's help (Friends give 1936; LighthouseFriends places it after August 1934).
Original Fresnel lens replaced with a plastic lens (Friends); the accounts of which lens is in Rockland differ.
Keeper's house bought by Jeff and Judi Burke and converted into an inn.
Tower and keeper's house registered as one unit, under separate owners (Friends); NRHP nomination prepared 1987.
Tower title passed to the Town of Isle au Haut under the Maine Lights Program (town vote 40-1).
Tower restored: scaffolding, brick replaced, lantern railing replicated.
Keeper's house and land bought by Marshall Chapman, who reopened it as an inn in 2013.
Inn closed after the 2018 season.
Knowles Industrial Services stabilized the foundation and tower walls.
Keeper's house sold for $1.3 million (LighthouseFriends); now a private residence.
Gallery deck repairs by JB Leslie Co.

notes_for_editor: Keeper's name: Elmer F. (USLHS) against Francis Elmer (LighthouseFriends) and Elmer (the Friends). The 1916 Commissioner list prints 'E. T. Holbrook' for the Isle au Haut keeper; the initials differ and the OCR column layout is hard to read (check the page image, scan 165, before relying on it). Daughter Esther's age at the Christmas Eve 1907 lighting: eight (LighthouseFriends, local tradition) against twelve (the Friends); the notice gives 30 December as the establishment date. The lighting story is unverified local tradition. Automation: 29 June 1933 (LighthouseFriends) against 1934 (NRHP, USLHS; the record). Keeper's house sale back to Robinson: August 1934 newspapers (LighthouseFriends) against 1936 (the Friends). Appropriation: $14,000 (NRHP, LighthouseFriends) against $14,400 (the Friends). Lens: fourth-order original (USLHS, LighthouseFriends); the Friends say the original was replaced with plastic in 1955 and rescued to a Rockland museum; LighthouseFriends says a fifth-order lens after automation is the one in the Maine Lighthouse Museum. The sources do not say which lens is in Rockland. Range: the 1908 notice gives 'twelve and one-third miles' (OCR 'oae-third'; check the image); the record's 6.0 nm is an ENC current value, not checked. The record's stay entry ('rental') is out of date: the Friends say the keeper's house is now a private residence and no longer an inn; correct the stay entry. The record's material 'brick' omits the granite base (NRHP, LighthouseFriends). The name 'Robinson Point' also appears in the Board's indexes for a light in Washington State; this station is on Robinson Point, Isle au Haut. Living people: the Burkes and Marshall Chapman are named as inn owners in their public role; Linda Greenlaw is named as the author of the cited book; the 2023 buyer and other private residents are not named. The 1916 assist entry is the only storm or rescue item for this station in the sources read. The 1906 Board report and the 1902 report quoted through LighthouseFriends are not in the corpus. The Ellsworth 1906 notice is an editorial paraphrase of the Board's recommendation; its quotations are as printed. Fact-check 2026-10-22: the 1916 "E. T. Holbrook" line (Commissioner FY1916, scan 165, printed p. 56) was matched by position in OCR text and the page image could not be opened from the checker, so the story hedges it; check the page image before relying on it. Esther Holbrook's lighting: Christmas Eve 1907 and age twelve (the Friends); age eight and Christmas Eve as local tradition, and New Year's Day 1908 from another source (LighthouseFriends); the notice gives 30 December as the establishment date. The story states all three. The 1936 Robinson buy-back is 1936 in the Friends and after August 1934 in LighthouseFriends; both are given. Linda Greenlaw (a living author and a relative of the former owner) is no longer named, per the living-people rule. Marshall Chapman is named only as the inn owner who presented himself publicly.
